target_customer: Software and SaaS companies that need to tell customers about downtime and incidents
problem: Companies handled outages with ad hoc tweets and support emails. StatusPage gave them hosted status pages with subscriber notifications and metrics.
business_model: SaaS subscription tiers, starting at 29 dollars per month in 2016

founders.name: Steve Klein
founders.background_notes: YC page: handled design and front-end development, growth and support; moved into product management at Atlassian.

founders.name: Danny Olinsky
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no bio found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A hosted web app with notifications and integrations; the main challenge was reliability since customers use it during their own outages.

defensibility.rationale: Subscriber lists and integrations create modest lock-in but the product is simple to copy; many alternatives launched around the same time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Atlassian was a long time partner and bought it in July 2016, its first acquisition after its IPO.

market_need_then: Cloud services were growing and companies needed a clear way to communicate outages. By 2016 it served thousands of customers including New Relic, Intuit and Venmo.

branding.domain_note: Used statuspage.io; now redirects to Atlassian.
branding.community_and_virality: Status pages on customer subdomains spread the brand through use; no merch or community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: The descriptive name became the category default word and public status pages exposed the brand to end users, though no source documents brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: StatusPage was a small capital efficient SaaS that reportedly stayed profitable, reached thousands of customers and was sold to Atlassian in July 2016 after years as an Atlassian partner. Its small seed funding and product led distribution through customer status pages suggest a bootstrapped style path. The price was not disclosed.
notes: No reliable funding data: aggregators conflict (20K to 100K seed, investors FundersClub, Wefunder, Atlassian), so none recorded as rounds. Profitability claim comes from a Hired profile snippet, unverified. YC page says founded 2012, others say 2013. No competitors dated near the batch found; Status.io is said to have launched in 2013 but the source is undated. Founder education and prior employers not found.
